detailed_rationale:
United Breweries (UBL) is India's largest beer company (Kingfisher, plus the Heineken portfolio under license/JV). Q4 FY26 - a seasonally strong summer quarter - showed revenue of Rs 2,250cr (up from Rs 2,073cr in Q3) and net profit of Rs 101.8cr, with sell-in volumes up 4.1% YoY and sell-out volumes up high-single-digits; premiumisation was the standout theme, with premium-segment volumes (Kingfisher Ultra, Kingfisher Ultra Max, Heineken Silver) up 16% YoY and roughly 80% of markets returning to growth as the overall beer category grew ~10%. FY26 full-year net profit came in at ~Rs 413cr. However, multiple trackers frame the quarter as 'margin pressures persist despite profit recovery' - a recurring theme for Indian beer companies, where many states regulate retail pricing/MRP directly, limiting the industry's ability to pass through rising input costs (barley/malt, glass and packaging) even when volumes and premium mix are improving.

The quant data shows this tension clearly: revenue growth is real but modest (7.2% 3-year CAGR, 3.6% trailing 1-year, both well below the seasonal Q4-quarter numbers seen in isolation), quality_score is low (21.7) reflecting a modest ~9.2% ROE for a supposedly strong consumer-staples brand, and value_score is low (20.7/100) against a rich ~86x trailing PE. Premiumisation is a genuine structural positive - it improves mix and margin per unit sold - but it is happening on a base where overall volume growth is only mid-single-digit and regulatory pricing constraints remain a persistent, structural drag on translating that mix-shift fully into bottom-line growth.
recommendation_rationale: Premiumisation is real and margin-accretive at the mix level, but overall volume and revenue growth remain modest, and state-level pricing regulation continues to cap how much of that premium mix-shift converts into margin expansion - management's own commentary on persistent margin pressure supports this. At ~86x trailing earnings for a business compounding revenue in the mid-single digits with sub-10% ROE, the valuation is not supported by the growth actually being delivered. We keep the quant Sell.
summary: United Breweries continues to grow its premium beer portfolio faster than the overall category, which is a genuine positive, but total volume and revenue growth remain modest and regulatory pricing constraints keep margins under pressure. At a rich valuation for the growth on offer, we recommend Sell.
positive_para: Premiumisation is a real and structurally attractive trend - Kingfisher Ultra, Ultra Max and Heineken Silver all grew volumes at double-digit rates in the most recent quarter, well ahead of the ~10% overall beer-category growth, and roughly 80% of UBL's markets returned to growth. This mix-shift should support margin improvement over time as premium products carry better unit economics.
negative_para: Overall volume growth is only mid-single-digit and multiple trackers describe margin pressure as persistent rather than resolved, reflecting the beer industry's structural exposure to state-level pricing regulation that limits pass-through of rising input costs. ROE of ~9.2% and a quality_score of 21.7/100 are unremarkable for a company trading at ~86x trailing earnings - a valuation that assumes considerably stronger compounding than the current growth and margin trajectory supports.
reverse_dcf_judgment: An ~86x trailing multiple on a beverage business growing revenue in the mid-single digits, with sub-10% ROE and structurally capped pricing power in many states, requires a level of sustained premiumisation-driven margin expansion that has not yet shown up decisively in the reported numbers. Judgment: rich.
